about: CHAIN reric_808 (Design/content/chains/reric_808.md): King Godfred destroys the Wends' market of Reric in the summer of 808 and carries its merchants to Sliesthorp (Annales regni Francorum 808). Fourteen cards, 798 to about 810. The spine's thread godfreds_market. A Wendish wax merchant (the spine's cast.dragomir) wants Frankish iron and a friend in the west; in the spring of 808 the king's ships are called out and a dealer in people (cast.asulf) knows where they are bound; the merchant can warn one man, warn the whole beach, count the booths for the king, or sell out and go; in high summer the sails come into the bay; those who are taken row north in the king's wake and are set down on the strand at Sliesthorp, where the king has a wall ordered; in 809 the king sends word to the emperor by merchants (true: ARF 809) and the house may carry it to Dorestad. Four endings: the king's new town (what really happened), faith kept with the Wend (the honest road), Reric holds (history changed: flag changed_reric_survives), and the king's finder (the beach sold). Progress is flags ch_reric_808_1 to _10 and the branch flags named in each note; the spine's flags gf_reric_friend and gf_warned are set where their meaning is met. Cards with weight 0 are reached only by 'schedule'. Every option's note names its outcome text in Data/writing/chain_reric_808.json. Written 6 Oct 2026; a draft for the user to overwrite.

cards.note: Step 1, the start (drawn at Reric, or at Sliesthorp where the Wend has come with wax, 798 to 807). Dragomir is the spine's cast.dragomir (invented), an Obodrite trader in wax, honey and furs; he speaks through an interpreter until he trusts you. Sources: Reric 'which by its tolls was of great profit to his kingdom' (Annales regni Francorum 808: chronicle_793.json 808-summer-reric-destroyed); Thrasco given the Saxons' land beyond the Elbe in 804 (ARF 804); Thionville 805 c. 7, merchants going to the Slavs to go no further than the named posts (Bardowick first) and to carry no arms (chronicle 805-12-thionville-border-posts): tools are not arms. Wax and honey are the Wends' goods (goods_793.json: wendland 3). Sets ch_reric_808_1; ch_reric_808_order if the order is taken.

cards.note: Step 3, and a second way into the chain (drawn at Sliesthorp, Ripa or Hleidr from spring to midsummer 808, whether or not step 1 was met). The king's ships are called out. Asulf is the spine's cast.asulf (invented), a dealer in captives who serves the king's wars. Sources: ARF 808: Godfred crossed with his army into the Obodrites' land; the Wilzi, old enemies of the Obodrites, joined him of their own will; the spine places the gathering of ships at Ripa and Sliesthorp. That a dealer bought fetters beforehand is ours. This is the warning before the danger (CHAINS.md rule 5). Sets ch_reric_808_3; ch_reric_808_knows when the merchant learns where the ships are bound; ch_reric_808_kings_offer when the king's man asks him to count the booths.

cards.note: Step 4 (drawn at Reric in 808 before July, by a merchant who knows where the ships are bound). The choice the chain turns on. Told alone, Dragomir puts his best goods in the merchant's boat to go west (flag ch_reric_808_goods: six cakes of wax and three timbers of marten, 600 d by the table, which are HIS). Told aloud, the beach may believe a Frisian or may not: ARF 808 says Thrasco fled 'distrusting the loyalty of his people', so a quarrelling beach is true to the year; if they believe, they carry their goods behind the island that shelters the bay (Poel) before the fleet comes (flag ch_reric_808_hid: history changed). Counted for the king, the booths are sold (flag ch_reric_808_counted; only if the king's man made the offer in step 3). Or the merchant sells out and goes (ch_reric_808_left). Sets ch_reric_808_4; gf_reric_friend when Dragomir is warned.

cards.note: Step 5, the event (drawn at Reric in July and August 808 with a weight that makes it sure; chronicle 808-summer-reric-destroyed fires on 1 August). Sources: ARF 808: before he went home Godfred destroyed the emporium on the shore which in the Danes' tongue was called Reric and which by its tolls was of great profit to his kingdom, and carrying the merchants off from there he weighed anchor and came with his whole army to the harbour called Sliesthorp; he had hanged Godelaib, another chief, taken by treachery; Thrasco had fled; Reginold, his brother's son, was killed at the storming of a stronghold with many Danish nobles. The danger was warned of in step 3. A Frisian is the emperor's man, and 808 to 810 are enemy years (realms/denmark.md): the plea rests on a gift. Sets ch_reric_808_5 and one of ch_reric_808_carried, ch_reric_808_slipped, ch_reric_808_pleaded; a merchant whose warning was believed may lie behind the island with the Wends.

cards.note: Step 7 (drawn at Sliesthorp on the first call after the burning, to the end of 810). The merchants of Reric are set down on the strand and the wall is ordered. Sources: ARF 808: at Sliesthorp the king stayed some days and decided to close the border of his kingdom toward Saxony with a rampart from the eastern bay to the western sea, along the north bank of the Eider, with one gate for wagons and horsemen, and shared the work among the leaders of his troops (chronicle 808-summer-danevirke). That plots were marked out for the newcomers is an inference from the planned look of Hedeby's earliest harbour settlement (?); that the merchants owed days at the wall is ours. Asulf (cast.asulf) has Wends in his pen; Ratimir, Dragomir's sister's son, is invented (Rati- + -mir, names_placeholder.json). This card chooses the road to an ending: the king's new town (ch_reric_808_road_town), faith kept with Dragomir (ch_reric_808_road_faith), or the finder's share (ch_reric_808_road_finder, only for one who counted the booths). Sets ch_reric_808_8.

cards.note: Step 8 (drawn at Sliesthorp from March to July 809, for any merchant who was in the story of the burning). True: in 809 Godfred sent word to the emperor 'by certain merchants' (per negotiatores quosdam, ARF 809) that he had heard the emperor was angry with him for leading an army against the Obodrites, that he wished to clear himself, that the others had broken the peace first, and asked for a meeting of counts beyond the Elbe; they met at Badenfliot and nothing came of it (chronicle 809-badenfliot). Who the merchants were is not said: here the house may be one of them. Sets ch_reric_808_9; ch_reric_808_word when the message is taken (schedules step 9 at Dorestad).

cards.note: ENDING 'the king's new town' (scheduled 240 days after step 7, at Sliesthorp: a winter held). What really happened: the merchants of Reric stayed where the king set them, and the market at the head of the Slie grew into Hedeby (ARF 808; ports_793.json sliesthorp). Lines by year: Thrasco killed at Reric by Godfred's men (ARF 809); Godfred killed by one of his own following and Hemming king (ARF 810); twelve men a side swear peace on the Eider (ARF 811). Grand reward: a charter of the king's word (unlock_charter_sliesthorp), unless the house told the count everything (ch_reric_808_two_tongues); or a plot (unlock_plot_sliesthorp); or a guest's standing (unlock_title_guest_on_the_slie). Cost that lasts: ch_reric_808_danes_man, counted a Dane's man by Franks and Frisians in the enemy years to 811. Sets ch_reric_808_end_new_town.

cards.note: ENDING 'faith kept' (scheduled 200 days after step 7, at Sliesthorp). The honest road: the goods got out are paid for, or a kinsman was bought free. Dragomir becomes a sworn partner with a boat of his own (unlock_partner_dragomir): partnership in a boat between men of different peoples is the Norse felag, known from the rune stones of the 10th and 11th centuries and assumed here for the 9th (?); the Svea trader who brings his kin's wax is the spine's cast.holmfast, his friend. The whole price paid is the hard road and gives a second grand reward, the silver temple ring his wife wore (unlock_heirloom_wend_temple_ring: such rings of twisted wire are the Wendish women's ornament in the spine's description; their 9th-century date is not checked (?)). A man with no silver may give his hand on it (unlock_factor_sliesthorp, and ch_reric_808_owes_dragomir). Sets ch_reric_808_end_kept_faith.

cards.note: ENDING 'Reric holds' (HISTORY CHANGED; drawn from September 808 at Reric or at any Baltic or Danish landing, where a Wend boat finds the merchant whose warning was believed). The booths burned empty; the merchants were behind the island; nobody was carried to the Slie, and the beach is built again. Sets changed_reric_survives. Under it: wells at Gross Stromkendorf with timbers felled as late as 811 (dendrochronology, de.wikipedia 'Reric', read 6 Oct 2026), and ARF 809, which still calls the place an emporium when Thrasco is killed there: something of Reric outlived 808 even as it happened. Grand rewards: a booth of the house's own on the new beach and a sworn partner (the hardest road: two), or the partner alone, or the Wends' pilotage of their bay (unlock_pilot_wendish_bay). Cost that lasts: ch_reric_808_godfred_enmity until the king is dead (810). The game must keep the port open when the flag is set: see 'needs' in the chain page. Sets ch_reric_808_end_reric_holds.

cards.title: Reric holds
cards.intention: A Wend boat lies at the landing with new wax in her and a face you know at the steering oar. Dragomir has been asking for a Frisian boat at every beach for a month.

cards.note: ENDING 'the king's finder' (scheduled 60 days after step 7, at Sliesthorp, for one who counted the booths). The beach sold. The taking is shared out when the wall is begun: the finder may have a Wendish boat that was rowed north by her owner (unlock_ship_baltic_coastal_boat, ship_classes_793.json), or a corner of Asulf's store (unlock_factor_sliesthorp), or the king's peace and silver (unlock_title_kings_peace_of_the_danes). That a king's man shared plunder with those who served him is the custom of every following; the Frankish law of 805 gives an informer a part of what is seized (Thionville c. 7), which is the nearest written rule and is not the Danes' (?). Cost that lasts: ch_reric_808_wend_feud (the Wends of the Slie will not deal with the house, and Dragomir remembers), and ch_reric_808_danes_man. Sets ch_reric_808_end_kings_finder.

cards.title: The finder's share
cards.intention: The taking of Reric is shared out on the strand, by tally, with a scale. The king's spokesman calls the leaders of the ships first, then the men who were useful.

options.note: outcome: chain_reric_808.s14.out_store (900 d by weight, and your goods lie beside his pen)
